thesis: Kratos is the affordable-mass arm of the US defense industrial base: jet-powered target and tactical drones (XQ-58 Valkyrie), hypersonic vehicles and solid rocket motors, small turbofan engines, microwave electronics and satellite ground software. Q2 2026 revenue grew 30.5% to $458.8 million (19.1% organic) with a 1.3-to-1 trailing book-to-bill, $2.084 billion backlog and a $15.0 billion bid pipeline, and management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.750-1.810 billion. The stock has fallen roughly 67% from its January 2026 high of $134 as a 15x-sales multiple reset, a ~$1.35 billion equity raise diluted shares ~21% year over year, and CCA airframe awards went largely to the primes. The offset is that GAAP profit is still negligible and free cash flow is guided to a use of $85-105 million in 2026 with heavy investment continuing into 2027, so the thesis rests on the 2027 hypersonics, engine and Valkyrie production ramp converting backlog into cash.

drivers: FY2027 revenue of ~$2.1-2.2B on guided 18-23% organic growth with adjusted EBITDA margin up another ~100bps to ~10.8%, implying ~$230M EBITDA
Hypersonics franchise scaling from ~$200M in 2025 toward $700M+ in 2027 on MACH-TB and the hoped-for ~$1B sole-source prime award
Valkyrie moving from prototypes to a program of record, ramping toward ~40 aircraft per year by the start of 2028, plus the Northrop-teamed USMC MUX TACAIR CCA
Small turbofan production ramp to 3,000 GEK-class engines in 2027 for cruise-missile demand, with GE Aerospace partnership de-risking the line
$1.44B cash and no funded debt let Kratos self-fund capacity while peers ration capital; analyst consensus targets sit near $98

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands inside guidance at $1.75-1.81B revenue and $173-176M adjusted EBITDA, FY2027 grows ~20% with modest margin expansion, and free cash flow stays negative through 2027 before inflecting in 2028. The market keeps Kratos at roughly 4-5x forward sales and ~40x forward EBITDA, rewarding backlog conversion but not paying a growth premium until cash generation turns.

risks: Free cash flow use persists beyond 2027 as capex, rocket-motor inventory and Valkyrie builds outrun definitized customer orders
Tactical drone and hypersonic awards slip or go to primes and non-traditional rivals such as Anduril, leaving invested capacity underutilized
GAAP earnings stay near zero while stock compensation of $60-64M a year and further equity issuance keep diluting shareholders
A DoW continuing resolution, shutdown or budget reprioritization delays funding as it did in late 2025 and early 2026
Shekel strength and fixed-price contract cost inflation cap margin expansion in the Israeli microwave and legacy target businesses

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results plus initial full-year 2027 guidance, including the first framed view of 2027 margins and cash flow
Management-flagged hope for an additional ~$1B hypersonic program opportunity believed to be sole source to Kratos as prime
Zeus and Oriole solid rocket motor deliveries begin arriving and ramp, unlocking recognized revenue on funded hypersonic work
GEK800 turbofan moves from first ignition (Sept 21, 2026, with GE Aerospace) toward a 3,000-engine annual production rate
Planned start of ~40 Valkyrie aircraft per year production rate, the key test of the loyal-wingman thesis

key_risks: Free cash flow use of $85-105M guided for FY2026 with heavy investment continuing into FY2027
GAAP operating income of only $16-22M on ~$1.78B of guided revenue leaves almost no earnings cushion
Diluted share count rose from 157.4M to 190.1M year over year after ~$1.35B of equity issuance in H1 2026
Tactical drone and hypersonic programs may not convert into programs of record on the expected schedule
Dependence on US Department of War budgets, appropriations timing and shutdown risk
Israeli Shekel strength and fixed-price contracts pressuring Microwave Products profitability
Integration and goodwill risk from the Nomad and Orbit acquisitions, with goodwill at $871.2M
